chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from al-Zurari ibn A'yan and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man marries four women and divorces one of them, he does not marry the fifth until the waiting period of the woman he divorced has expired.
And he said: He does not combine his water in five.

key_terms.عِدَّةُ: Waiting period (iddah) after divorce or death

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a man to marry a fifth wife according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the maximum limit of four wives and the condition for a fifth, emphasizing that the prohibition on holding five simultaneously applies only after the first divorce is finalized. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that 'water' (semen/offspring) is not combined in more than five, implying a potential exception or specific legal nuance regarding the fifth wife compared to the standard four. The ruling underscores the importance of the *iddah* period in maintaining clear lineage and marital status before expanding the household further.
